subject.title: [Feature]: cron add: support custom job IDs via --id

question: Should OpenClaw accept caller-supplied cron job IDs at creation time as a public CLI/Gateway/agent-tool contract, and what validation/collision rules should that contract use?
rationale: The code path is small, but the change makes a new user-controlled stable identifier part of the cron API and affects CLI, protocol schema, service persistence, run-log safety, and model-facing cron tool behavior.

options.title: Accept custom IDs with a narrow contract
options.body: Approve an optional explicit ID field with conservative slug validation, duplicate rejection, docs, and coverage across CLI, Gateway protocol, service, and agent-tool surfaces.

options.title: Keep UUID-only creation
options.body: Reject create-time custom IDs and instead improve list/show/edit ergonomics around generated IDs, leaving this feature request closed by maintainer direction later.

options.title: Defer to broader declarative cron work
options.body: Hold this until a wider cron GitOps/import model settles identifiers across CLI, files, and automation.

recommendation.title: Accept custom IDs with a narrow contract
recommendation.body: Approve an optional explicit ID field with conservative slug validation, duplicate rejection, docs, and coverage across CLI, Gateway protocol, service, and agent-tool surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a public cron CLI/Gateway contract decision and the recent history shows this owner reviewing or carrying adjacent cron CLI/protocol work.
